name: room
text: Room opened — goal: visualization: Own the VISUAL PRESENTATION of the interface — visibility, liveliness, clarity, enjoyment

name: Facet
text: We should create interactive slides using Google Slides to own the visual presentation of the interface. This approach allows for a dynamic and engaging presentation that can be easily updated and shared, which supports the goal of liveliness and enjoyment. By choosing Google Slides, we trade off the ability to create highly customized designs, but gain the benefits of a widely accessible and collaborative platform. This trade-off is acceptable because it prioritizes clarity and visibility, making it easier for our audience to follow and understand the presentation.

name: Pane
text: Google Slides is a display tool, not an interactive one—it can’t simulate real interface behavior. The real risk is mistaking polished slides for a living demo, which fails the liveliness and clarity tests. A better alternative is a clickable prototype in Figma or Framer, where users can *feel* the interface’s rhythm. Settle it by building a 3-screen prototype and timing how long it takes a first-time user to complete a core task—if it’s under 30 seconds, the slides are dead weight.
